name: Meridian Trust Bank ARB design review, US
out_of_profile: contract clause matching (contracts live in the legal system)
bare retention numbers (banks cite a Records Retention Schedule class)

controls.title: Approved services only
controls.requirement: Every cloud service and third-party component named in the design must be on the Approved Cloud Services Catalog, or the package must reference an approved exception by id. The package must contain a list of services and components with their catalog status. A component named in the design but missing from the list is a finding.
controls.applicability: Applies to every new application and material change. Not applicable only to documentation-only changes with no deployed component.

framework_map.status: illustrative; not reviewed by a compliance owner
ffiec_is_booklet: II.C.5 Inventory and classification of assets

controls.reviewer_role: ARB reviewer, Data Governance and Third-Party Risk
required_clauses: every cloud service and component is listed
catalog status or exception id is given for each item

controls.title: Data classification and regulatory scope per data store
controls.requirement: Every data store must carry a classification label under IS-STD-003: Public, Internal, Confidential or Restricted. Stores holding nonpublic personal information must be flagged NPI (GLBA). If payment card data could be present, the design must state the PCI DSS scope boundary.
controls.applicability: Applies whenever the application stores or processes data. Not applicable only to stateless components that hold no data at rest.

framework_map.status: illustrative; not reviewed by a compliance owner
ffiec_is_booklet: II.C.5 Inventory and classification of assets
glba_occ: Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards (12 CFR 30, App. B)

controls.reviewer_role: ARB reviewer, Data Governance and Third-Party Risk
required_clauses: classification label given per data store

controls.title: Authentication and MFA via enterprise IdP
controls.requirement: All human access, for users and administrators, must authenticate through the enterprise IdP. Multi-factor authentication is required, and it must be phishing-resistant for privileged and remote access. The application must not keep local user accounts.
controls.applicability: Applies to every component with a human access path. Not applicable to components reached only by workload identities.

framework_map.status: illustrative; not reviewed by a compliance owner
glba_occ: FFIEC Authentication and Access to Financial Institution Services and Systems (2021)

controls.reviewer_role: ARB reviewer, Data Governance and Third-Party Risk

controls.title: Least privilege, PAM, no shared admin, break-glass named
controls.requirement: Access must use named roles scoped to specific resources. Privileged access must be brokered through the enterprise PAM vault, and there must be no shared administrator account. A break-glass path must be named, require two-person approval, and expire.
controls.applicability: Applies to every application with production accounts or administrative interfaces.
evidence: Architecture document, privileged access section and role table

framework_map.status: illustrative; not reviewed by a compliance owner

controls.reviewer_role: ARB reviewer, Technology Resilience and Operations
required_clauses: break-glass named with two-person approval and expiry

controls.title: Encryption at rest and key management
controls.requirement: All customer data at rest must be encrypted with AES-256. Keys must be AWS KMS customer-managed keys or held in CipherTrust Manager; provider-managed or default keys do not meet this requirement. Keys must rotate at least annually, and the key custodians must be named.
controls.applicability: Applies to every data store holding Confidential or Restricted data. Not applicable only if the classification document shows no such data at rest.
evidence: Architecture document, encryption at rest and key management section

framework_map.status: illustrative; not reviewed by a compliance owner

required_clauses: key management model stated (AWS KMS customer-managed keys or CipherTrust)

controls.title: Security events to enterprise SIEM (Splunk)
controls.requirement: Security events from control plane, network flow, application audit and model invocation sources must be forwarded to the enterprise SIEM (Splunk). Retention must follow IS-STD-021. A named team must own the alerts raised on these events.
controls.standard: IS-STD-021 Security Logging and Monitoring v3.0 §4
evidence: Architecture document, logging and monitoring section

framework_map.status: illustrative; not reviewed by a compliance owner

controls.reviewer_role: ARB reviewer, Technology Resilience and Operations
required_clauses: security event sources forwarded to Splunk

controls.title: Third parties named with TPRM assessment id and inherent risk tier
controls.requirement: Every third party or sub-processor in the design must be named and must carry a TPRM assessment id and an inherent risk tier. Each assessment must be current on the date of review.
controls.applicability: Applies whenever the design uses a third party or sub-processor. Not applicable only if the design states that no third party is used and no document in the package names one.

framework_map.status: illustrative; not reviewed by a compliance owner

controls.reviewer_role: ARB reviewer, Data Governance and Third-Party Risk

controls.title: RTO/RPO consistent with BIA tier, rollback path, immutable backups
controls.requirement: The package must state RTO and RPO, and both must be consistent with the application's BIA tier. A rollback path for deployments must be described. Backups must be immutable, for example held in a vault-locked backup vault. Evidence may be in the architecture document or the runbook.
controls.applicability: Applies to every production application with a BIA tier.

glba_occ: Interagency Paper on Sound Practices to Strengthen Operational Resilience (2020)
